clue.text: One dressed in purple finding old javelin

indicators.note: a thing dressed in clothing sits inside it, so the numeral goes within the colour

parts.note: plum is a deep purple colour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone clad in purple turns up carrying an ancient spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' puts I inside PLUM. The pilum was the heavy throwing spear of the Roman legionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilum was the standard spear thrown by Roman soldiers, hence an old javelin.

clue.text: Land in gym before football game

indicators.note: before puts the piece for gym ahead of the piece for the game

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
RU is rugby union, a football code

explanation.surface: A country where the gym session comes ahead of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country in South America, so it is an example of a land.

clue.text: Girl fortunate to have avoided work, ultimately

indicators.note: avoiding something means staying clear of it, so that letter is left out of the word for fortunate

parts.note: lucky means fortunate

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of work is taken

explanation.surface: A girl was lucky enough to get out of doing any work in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives K, the last letter of 'work'; 'to have avoided' removes it from LUCKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucy is a girl's name, so it fits the general term girl.

clue.text: Preserve horse for transporting mother and boy

indicators.note: a horse transporting riders carries them, so the other pieces sit inside the word for horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
ma is mother
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A horse carries a mother and her son, perhaps with jam for the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus fruit preserve, usually made from oranges.

clue.text: Most obscure desk art rubbished

indicators.note: to rubbish something is to trash it, so the letters of these two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the most obscure art made from a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbished' rearranges DESKART into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkest is the superlative of dark, in the sense of hardest to see or understand: most obscure.

clue.text: Overrides a decision to include controversial nobleman

indicators.note: the words include the answer, which runs through them across word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone overturns a ruling to let a scandalous aristocrat in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' says the answer sits inside 'Overrides a decision'. The Marquis de Sade was a notorious 18th-century French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Sade was a French aristocrat whose writings caused scandal; sadism takes his name.

clue.text: Legendary bird's goodness recalled

indicators.note: recalled read as called back says the word is taken back to front

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like goodness

explanation.surface: A mythical bird's virtue is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns COR, a British cry of surprise, into ROC. The roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a huge mythical bird in Middle Eastern tales such as Sinbad's voyages.

clue.text: Climb initially into exotic tea tree and rest

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other
exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of climb is used

explanation.surface: Climb a strange tea tree, then take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives C; 'exotic' rearranges TEATREE into ETETERA; 'into' puts C inside to make the answer. 'rest' looks like relaxation but means the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera means and the rest, the remaining things of the same kind.

clue.text: Most meagre pub in the street

indicators.note: in places the word for pub inside the word the

parts.note: taken as its letters
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: The poorest pub in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinnest means slightest or scantiest, the superlative sense of meagre.

clue.text: Chronicles concerned with trousers

parts.note: re means about, regarding, as in a letter heading
cords are corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: Historical accounts that deal with legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronicles are written accounts of events in order, which are records; both work as verbs too.

clue.text: Their sharp points scratch this, at intervals?

definitions.text: Their sharp points scratch this, at intervals?

indicators.note: taking letters at intervals means every other letter of the two words, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A riddle: what plants have spines that would scratch you?
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of SCRATCH THIS spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: spiny plants that scratch whoever brushes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are desert plants covered in spines whose sharp points scratch anyone who touches them.

clue.text: Railway station put out some pop, adding to noise

indicators.note: put out some says a portion of the following words is displayed: the answer is a run of letters hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A London terminus broadcasts some pop music, making the din worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'put out' into the definition, but no station is 'put out'; 'put out some' is the indicator, saying a portion of the next words is shown. PADDINGTON is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is one of London's main-line rail termini, serving the west of England.

clue.text: In no atlas, strangely, will you find a country's inhabitants

indicators.note: strangely means oddly arranged, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An atlas, oddly, fails to show where a nation's people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges INNOATLAS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a particular nation, i.e. a country's people.

clue.text: Function venue one used to sweep round completely

indicators.note: a thing placed round another surrounds it, so the broom word wraps the word for completely

parts.note: a broom is used for sweeping
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A hall for events where the cleaner sweeps right round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like purpose but means a formal party or dance; 'round' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall for dances and formal functions.

clue.text: Submarine, perhaps, making for Kentish port once

definitions.meaning: a submarine is a long filled roll, a kind of sub snack
a town in Kent that was one of the Cinque Ports but is now inland as the sea retreated

explanation.surface: A navy submarine heading for an old harbour in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' suggests a vessel, but it is the long sandwich called a sub. Sandwich is a town in Kent, England, once a Cinque Port and now inland.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a type of long filled roll, and Sandwich is a former port town in Kent.

clue.text: Girl going with sailor to see film

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
tar is an old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A young woman and a seaman go out to the cinema together.
explanation.walkthrough: AVATAR is James Cameron's 2009 science-fiction blockbuster.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is the title of a famous 2009 James Cameron movie, so the answer is an example of a film.

clue.text: Gazes fixedly, flight being heard

indicators.note: being heard says the word for a flight is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a flight of steps is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone watches an aircraft intently while it can be heard overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like aircraft or escape, but here it is a flight of stairs; 'being heard' turns STAIRS into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare is to look fixedly, so the plural verb matches gazes fixedly.

clue.text: Voting system is possible as form of punishment!

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
on means feasible, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: A wry claim that an electoral system can itself be a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisonment, being locked up in jail, is a common sentence, hence a form of punishment.

clue.text: Admires loo after refurbishment: this one?

definitions.text: Admires loo after refurbishment: this one?

indicators.note: a refurbished room is rearranged and redone, so the letters of these two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admires a freshly done-up toilet and wonders which one it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after refurbishment' rearranges ADMIRESLOO into the answer, and the whole clue points to a women's lavatory as the loo in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' room is a women's public lavatory, which is the kind of loo the question asks about.

clue.text: Relative's jibe when head goes missing

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which goes missing

parts.note: a taunt is a jibe

explanation.surface: A family member's insult loses its sting when its beginning is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when head goes missing' takes the first letter T off TAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, so she is a family relative.

clue.text: Difficult set

definitions.meaning: become firm, as concrete or jelly that has set

explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is read as an adjective: concrete that has set is solid.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer means not easy, and also firm or solid, as something that has set.

clue.text: After work, I'm swallowing universal painkiller

indicators.note: the second part follows the first, so the piece for work comes first

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: something swallowed goes inside, so the U letter goes within the letters of I'm

parts.note: taken as its letters I and M
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their shift and takes a pain pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' makes IUM; 'After' signals that this follows the piece for work, op being short for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic from poppies, historically used to dull pain, so it is a painkiller.

clue.text: Old woman, cold, finds coat

parts.note: ma, like old woman, is informal for mother
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chilly mother finds herself a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is British slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a British word for a raincoat.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil put, alas, in the wrong places

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong places have been shuffled out of order, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook laments a kitchen tool left in the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong places' rearranges PUTALAS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed tool for lifting and spreading food in cooking.

clue.text: Medic greeting Rod's short hairstyle

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a military doctor
hi is a greeting

indicators.note: short means cut down at the end, so the last letter comes off the word for a rod

parts.note: a rod is a cane; the 's is just 'is' joining it to short

explanation.surface: A doctor says hello to Rod, who has a short haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CANE to CAN. 'Rod' looks like a man's name, but it is the stick. A Mohican is a strip of upright hair down the middle of a shaved head.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican (US: mohawk) is a hairstyle with a central crest and shaved sides.

clue.text: Auditor's seen in place

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this signals the word for seen is taken by its sound

parts.note: sighted means seen, spotted

explanation.surface: A financial auditor has been spotted somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it is literally a hearer. 'in place' works as 'put in place', a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sited has been positioned or located, i.e. put in place.
